2. Material facts of the case as necessary for disposal of the Rule are that the opposite —1 party Nos.1-5 as plaintiffs filed a suit being Title Suit No.136 of 1998 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession and also for declaration that the judgment and decree dated 15.6.1998 passed in Title Suit No.7 of 1995 by the same Court was collusive and not binding upon the plaintiffs on the averments that the suit land along with other lands were originally belonged to Sudhir Chandra Dutta and Subid Chandra Dutta, the Proforma-defendant Nos. 4-5 who while possessing in equal share comprising 0.3603 acre out of .7206 acres of land in plot No.5137 transferred their share to Most. Jahurunnessa Khanam (proforma defendant No.3) by registered kabala No.15310 dated 15.11.1989 corresponding to 1st Agrahayan, 1396 B.S. at a consideration of Tk. 85.000/00, subsequently who in necessity of money transferred the said land in favotir of the plaintiffs through his 'attorney, Ishtiaque Khaled by a registered deed dated 5.10.97 and defendant No.2, Monjur Ahmed transferred his share to plaintiff No.5, Md. Abdul Wadud by executing a registered-deed dated 7.9.98 and accordingly, the plaintiff Nos. 1-5 became exclusive owner of the suit land; that entire land of the suit plot including the structure thereon was requisitioned by the then Government on 26.9.47 from the ,defendant Nos. 4-7, the original owner of the land including the suit land for the purpose of residence and office of the Government officials and employees; that out of .7206 acre of suit plot, the then Zaminder Khan Bahadur Dewan Eklimur Raja of Sylhet town purchased .1801 acre of suit plot and one Muzibur Rahman purchased .1801 acre of suit plot; that the defendant Nos. 4-5 while possessing .3606 acre out of which in southern portion .1650 acre was acquired by the defendant No.1, Deputy Conimissioner, Sylhet in L.A. Case No.14/69-70 for Agricultural Development Bank and rest .1927' acres remained under possession of the plaintiffs by purchase; that the suit land situated within the Zindabazar Commercial Area of Sylhet town and the structure, houses standing thereon were old of 50/60 years approximately; that the building was not useable as dwelling house and for construction of multistoried commercial building and market the plaintiffs purchased the land; that the plaintiffs by purchase acquired title over total 0.1927 acre; that the plaintiffs applied for de-requisition of their purchased land and to pay all arrear of rent enclosing all the relevant documents relating. to their ownership of the suit land but after long lapse of time the land acquisition officer in the middle part of May, 1998 all on a sudden disclosed that the plaintiffs have no right ownership in the suit land and as such question of de-requisition does not arise at all which cast a cloud over the title of the plaintiffs; that the defendant 'No.9, Md. Nazrul Islam has no right, title and possession over the suit land, who beyond the knowledge of the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.7 of 1995 and on 22.6.98 obtained a collusive decree by practicing fraud upon the Court which is not binding upon the plaintiffs, hence the suit. 

 7. Mr. Goutam Kumar Roy, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the petitioner submits that the Court of appeal below acted illegally in dismissing the suit and affirming the judgment of the trial Court below without considering the additional evidence as adduced before it. He next A relying on the decisions reported in 6 BLD (AD) 342 and 24 BLD(AD) 56 submits that admittedly the property in question was requisitioned by the then Pakistan Government and the plaintiff after failing to get back the suit property by way of de-requisition filed the instant suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession and in view of the bar imposed by the provisions of section 14A of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 the suit was not maintainable. 

 8. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Mahbub Ali, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1-5 upon referring the prayer portion of the plaint submits that the argument of the teamed Deputy Attorney General in the facts and circumstances of the case with regard to maintainability of the suit is plainly misconceived inasmuch as in this case the plaintiffs having not challenged the so-called requisition order of the then Pakistan Government. He adds that in the cited decisions namely the decisions reported in 6 BLD(AD) 342 and 24 BLD(AD) 56 the order of requisition of the suit property under section 3 of the (Emergency) Requisition Property Act, 1948 was challenged but in the present case it is apparent from the prayer portion of the plaint that the suit was filed for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession and as such the principles laid down in those cited cases are not applicable in the present case. 

 "Appellants who are plaintiffs filed O.S. No.19 of 1977 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong misleading respondent No.1 as defendant No.1 along with other defendants for a decree for establishment of title and confirmation possession with a prayer for permanent injunction and alternately  for khas possession on setting-aside an  order of requisition of the suit property  under section 3 of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948. Plaintiffs also filed an application under Order 39 Rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for temporary injunction restraining defendants from dispossessing them till the disposal of the suit." 

 "In the foregoing facts and circumstances of the case the petitioner's valid purchase of the property from the said Sushil Kumar Gangali remains undisputed until now. This is quite evident from the order passed on 15.3.77 by Mr. M. A. Samad, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms of the Government of Bangladesh, wherein it was held that the petitioner's property was never listed as a vested property nor was it made khas property of the Government. In such circumstances it was further ordered that it was not necessary to treat the property in question to be under any unauthorized possession of the petitioner and on that account the petitioner's eviction was avoided. It is surprising to note that only after four months on 22.7.77 another order was passed by Mr. S. Hossain. Khan, Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Land Administration and Reforms of the Government of Bangladesh wherein it was held that the property in question appeared to have been held as vested property and on 15.3.77 was reviewed and revised. In passing the subsequent order of 22.7.77 it was observed that the petitioner's title in the property in question was doubtful. Apart from the act that the petitioners title is based upon valid purchase of the property by a duly registered deed. The authority in the Government could not question and annul the validity of such title by an executive order. If the Government wanted to claim in such Property if could only do so by way of an appropriate suit for declaration of title and cancellation of the petitioner's registered kabala as such. Be that as it may it is surprising to note that a Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Land Reforms could revise an order passed only four months before by his predecessor, another Joint Secretary in the said Ministry of land Administration and Land Reforms. The subsequent order passed by joint Secretary Mr. S. Hossain Khan on 22.7.77 is obviously based on Illegal assumption of fact and as such suffers from clear illegality."
